description: PRD-106: Outcome Telemetry & Learning Foundation — Full research + design PRD. Study experiment tracking, observability, and recommendation patterns. Design telemetry capture that enables future learning without over-engineering.

userStories.title: Research experiment tracking and observability
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to study how production systems capture and query outcome data so that our telemetry is useful
acceptanceCriteria: Study MLflow experiment tracking — runs, metrics, parameters, artifacts, comparison queries
Study Weights & Biases — run logging, hyperparameter tracking, visualization, sweeps
Study Honeycomb observability — high-cardinality events, trace-based analysis, SLOs
Study OpenTelemetry spans — structured trace data, attributes, events, links
Study A/B testing frameworks — experiment design, metric collection, statistical significance
Comparison table: system, data model, query capabilities, scale, cost
Write to PRD section: '## 2. Prior Art: Outcome Tracking & Observability'
Identify which patterns are overkill vs essential for our scale
userStories.notes: PRD-100 philosophy: 'No fancy learning engine — just data. Query it for patterns later.' Honor this. We need structured data capture, not an ML pipeline. The question is: what data structure enables the queries we'll want later?

userStories.title: Design telemetry data model
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need the telemetry data model designed so that every mission outcome is queryable
acceptanceCriteria: Decision: separate mission_telemetry table vs JSONB on orchestration_tasks — recommend with rationale

Define per-task telemetry fields: agent_id, agent_type, model_used, tools_invoked (array), tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, cost_usd, duration_ms, retries, verifier_score, human_accepted (bool), error_type (nullable)
Define per-run aggregate fields: total_cost, total_tokens, total_duration, task_count, success_rate, average_verifier_score
Define indexing strategy for common queries
Write to PRD section: '## 3. Telemetry Data Model'
Include example data for a complete mission (3-4 tasks)
Address retention: how long to keep detailed telemetry, when to aggregate
userStories.notes: If using JSONB on orchestration_tasks (from PRD-101), telemetry is just additional fields on existing tables — no new migration needed. If separate table, it's cleaner but more complex. The right answer depends on query patterns (US-003).

userStories.title: Design query patterns and analytics
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need to define what questions the telemetry should answer so that the data model supports them
acceptanceCriteria: Define 10+ query patterns the telemetry must support:
1. Best model for research tasks (by verifier score)
2. Average cost per mission type
3. Which agents have highest human acceptance rate
4. Failure patterns by tool (which tools cause most retries)
5. Cost efficiency: tokens per quality point
6. Time breakdown: planning vs execution vs verification
7. Model comparison: same task type across different models
8. Agent utilization: how often each roster agent is assigned
9. Contractor vs roster agent performance comparison
10. Mission complexity vs actual cost (estimation accuracy)
Write SQL for each query pattern
Write to PRD section: '## 4. Query Patterns & Analytics'
Verify each query is executable against the proposed schema
userStories.notes: These queries are the REAL deliverable of this PRD. If the data model can't answer these questions, it's wrong. Write the queries first, then validate the schema supports them.

userStories.title: Design learning foundation
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need to define how raw telemetry enables future learning without building the learning engine yet
acceptanceCriteria: Define 'learning foundation' — what data patterns would enable: model routing optimization, agent selection improvement, cost prediction, failure prediction
Define minimum data volume needed before learning is meaningful (100+ missions? 1000+?)
Design data export format for future ML pipeline consumption (CSV, Parquet, or API)
Define privacy considerations — what to NEVER store (user content, PII), what to always store (metadata only)
Write to PRD section: '## 5. Learning Foundation'
Include roadmap sketch: telemetry → dashboards → manual insights → automated recommendations → dynamic optimization
Explicitly mark where Phase 2 ends and future work begins
userStories.notes: This is where we draw the line. Phase 2 captures data. Phase 2 does NOT build recommendation engines, dynamic model routing, or automated optimization. Those are future PRDs that consume this data. Make that boundary crystal clear.

userStories.title: Design telemetry dashboard
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a telemetry dashboard designed so that users can see mission outcomes at a glance
acceptanceCriteria: Define dashboard views: mission summary, cost breakdown, agent performance, model comparison
Define key metrics to display: total missions, success rate, average cost, average duration, top agents
Connect to existing Activity page — telemetry as a new tab or section
Define API endpoints needed: GET /api/telemetry/summary, GET /api/telemetry/missions/{id}
Write to PRD section: '## 6. Telemetry Dashboard'
Include wireframe sketches (ASCII) for summary view
Keep scope minimal — dashboard is a viewer, not an analytics tool
userStories.notes: The existing Activity page has Dashboard, Feed, Reports, Missions tabs. Telemetry could be a section within Dashboard or a new tab. Don't over-design the UI — a simple table with filters is fine for Phase 2.

userStories.title: Write PRD-106 complete document
userStories.description: As a document author, I need to write the complete PRD-106 document
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/106-OUTCOME-TELEMETRY.md
Header, Problem Statement, synthesis of US-001 through US-005
Design Decisions Made table
Risk Register (data volume, query performance, premature optimization)
Implementation Acceptance Criteria
Appendix: Full SQL schema for telemetry
Appendix: All 10 query patterns with SQL
Appendix: API endpoint specifications
Final review pass
PRD-106 complete and ready for peer review
userStories.notes: Follow PRD-100 style. This PRD should feel like a data engineering spec, not a product spec. The audience is whoever builds the telemetry tables and queries.
